w: Built into Sedona's red-rock buttes between 1954 and 1956, this chapel was commissioned by rancher and sculptor Marguerite Brunswig Staude and designed by August K. Strotz of the firm Anshen & Allen. Set within Coconino National Forest, it earned a place on the National Register of Historic Places in 2011.
s: A modernist chapel built into Sedona's red rock
_facts: Built 1954-1956 into red-rock buttes in Coconino National Forest
Commissioned by rancher and sculptor Marguerite Brunswig Staude
Designed by August K. Strotz of Anshen & Allen
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2011

w: One of Arizona's most photographed sights, this sandstone butte rises to 4,967 feet in Coconino National Forest. Carved from the Permian Schnebly Hill formation, once coastal dunes of an ancient sea, its steep trail shows ripple marks and a basalt dike. Early maps confused it with neighboring Courthouse Butte.
_facts: Summit elevation 4,967 feet, carved from Permian Schnebly Hill sandstone
Popular steep trail (USFS #170) climbs to the saddle points
Once called Court House Rock, confused with neighboring Courthouse Butte
A black basalt dike is visible in the first saddle along the trail

w: Seven miles north of Sedona in Oak Creek Canyon, this park is named for a natural water slide worn into slippery red sandstone by Oak Creek. Co-managed with the US Forest Service, it holds a 43-acre working apple farm and draws over a quarter million visitors a year.
s: A natural rock waterslide in Oak Creek Canyon
_facts: Named for a natural water slide in Oak Creek's sandstone bed
Co-managed by Arizona State Parks and the US Forest Service

w: A 286-acre state park five miles southwest of Sedona, built around a red sandstone canyon along Oak Creek. Its main mission is preserving riparian habitat rather than recreation, and it doubles as an environmental education facility for schools and the public, with only limited passive recreation on offer.
s: A red-sandstone canyon park preserving Oak Creek's habitat
_facts: 286 acres of red sandstone canyon along Oak Creek
Primary mission is riparian habitat preservation
Serves as an environmental education facility for schools
